findings.title: two skills still tell agents check-module does not exist, and this is the commit that makes it mandatory
findings.failure_scenario: milestone/SKILL.md: 'check-coverage, check-mutants and check-module do not exist until the Gradle build lands in M0 ... the report must say so every time'. tdd/SKILL.md: 'scripts/check-module.sh <module> green (see AGENTS.md -- does not exist until the build does)'. Both date to M-1.2 (965dc44); the build landed in M0.4 and the script in M0.5, and this commit puts the gate on every git commit. Failure scenario: an agent following the milestone skill reports check-module as an absent gate while it gated every commit in the milestone -- a false claim about a gate, which is non-negotiable 4 and the rule AGENTS.md says every other rule rests on. This is the same defect class the M0.5 commit body describes catching in AGENTS.md ('the generated Gates table said check-module.sh exists while the hand-written paragraph four lines below still listed it under Not yet existing'); the guard built for it is anchored on AGENTS.md's 'Not yet existing' paragraph and does not see .agents/skills/. Two one-line edits, no test surface. Recording per rule 11, or fold into M0.20 which is already the cross-reference scan.

findings.title: the --print-rules comment claims a property it does not have: RuleListTest is still a function of the index
findings.failure_scenario: The dispatch was moved above the 'no module changed' early exit, and its comment says so -- but it still sits below the drift halt at line 226 ('[ "$PLAN_DRIFT" = ok ] || finish'). Failure scenario: stage a new module directory containing build.gradle.kts before adding it to settings.gradle.kts -- an ordinary WIP state, and exactly what aTrackedOrphanFails asserts is drift -- and 'scripts/check-module.sh --print-rules' exits 1 having printed nothing. RuleListTest.everyModuleNamedByARuleStillExists then fails with 'NO_HTTP not printed by the gate' instead of anything about rule lists, and theRuleListsDoNotOverlap fails the same way. The window is narrower than the one that was fixed, but the comment's claim is stronger than the code: moving the dispatch above line 226 (it reads only literals assigned at 234/236, so nothing upstream is needed) would make the comment true. Correctness-of-claims finding under review.md rule 6.

notes: Q1 -- the split removes nothing check-module.sh depends on. No tracked reference to printTestInputs or print-inputs survives outside the M0.24 backlog row; check-module.sh touches buildSrc only as a string in the shared-build pattern and the drift skip. The two retained pieces are the load-bearing ones: '*.sh' in harnessScripts (ModuleGateTest copies check-module.sh and lib.sh, ModulePlanTest/ModuleSelectionTest/ModuleDriftTest exec them) and the rootSettings input plus the settings.gradle.kts pathspec (RuleListTest, ModulePlanTest.EIGHT and ModuleListDerivationTest all read the real module list). The drift fixtures sit at depth 6 so they cannot be seen by the depth-1 orphan grep, and they live under buildSrc/ so touching them escalates correctly.

Q2 -- the '-' sentinel is correct in every case I could construct. Verified by running the script: (A) --root at a tree whose settings names modules but which has no depth-1 build file yields cand='' and produces exactly the two true ghost FAILs, with no leakage of this repository's format/plugin/binstore-backends; (B) same via --check-drift, exit 1; (C) the real root still takes the '-' branch and reports DRIFT=ok checked=8 from the tracked set; (D) a settings file with no include block gives ALL= and checked=0. The one soft spot is (E): --root at a nonexistent directory prints 'DRIFT=ok checked=0' and exits 0, because cd fails into an empty cand and sed fails into an empty ALL. Existing tests are safe (ModuleDriftTest asserts the fixture dir exists, ModulePlanTest asserts checked=2 and checked=8), but a future fixture with a typo'd path would pass silently. Nit, not a finding.

Q3 -- NOT VERIFIED, and I am saying so rather than assuming. The commit body is not part of the staged diff and .git/COMMIT_EDITMSG still holds M0.5's message, so I have no text to judge. What the body must carry to be honest about this diff: the derivation rewrite closes M0.5's accepted M11/MT14 finding, which M0.5's own body says was to close with M0.6, so it is carried scope rather than new scope; the 'and CI' half of the task is not delivered here and is carried in the edited M0.7 row; the AGENTS.md row 'CI sets GATE_SCOPE=full to build all eight' is written in the present tense about a CI that does not exist in the tree, consistent with the rest of that table but still a forward-dated claim; ModuleGateTest's own header states that nothing in the repository asserts architecture.md rules 2, 4 or 5 (M0.23); and is_shared_build_change carries a self-declared untested guard ('this comment is the guard; there is no test').

Cost lens: no object-store request path is touched. The gate's own request rate is Gradle invocations and scales with modules built -- zero for a docs-only or script-only commit (verified: the delta branch exits at 'no module changed' before any gradlew call), one module per changed module directory, all eight on a shared-build change. That scales with modules, never with records, shards, partitions or indices.

Vacuous-pass lens: the wiring cannot pass while checking nothing in the ways that matter. pass_filenames:false is required and present -- with it true, pre-commit's filenames would land in the '$# -gt 0' named-module branch and every commit would FAIL with 'unknown module: docs'. DRIFT_CHECKED is a positive ran-signal rather than a did-not-fail signal, and ModulePlanTest pins it to 2 and 8. The rule counters take three distinct values per rule across the suite (0/1/4 and 0/1/2), which no constant satisfies. One latent fragility, not reachable today: lib.sh's fail() assigns FAILED=1 rather than incrementing, so plan()'s 'before'/'-eq' comparison would report PLAN_DRIFT=ok if anything had already failed before check_drift ran; today every earlier failure calls finish, so nothing reaches it.
